Items.Authors: Will Saunders, Corentin Cudennec, Roland Bacon, Philippe Dierickx, Roelof de Jong, David Lee, Gaston Gausachs
Items.Title: Alternative designs for the Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope
Items.Abstract: The Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope is proposed as the next large ESO project after ELT, combining Multi Object Spectroscopy and Integral Field Spectroscopy, each with order-of-magnitude gains over current systems. It has 12m aperture and 2 degree field-of-view, giving it an etendue larger than all fully-steerable MOS telescopes in history, combined, as well as having a simultaneous IFS focus. Costs are likely to be dominated by the spectrographs, and for MOS, the cost per unit science varies steeply with the delivered image quality. Hence, notwithstanding the challenging etendue, exceptional delivered image quality is paramount. Several telescope designs were developed, differentiated mostly by the M2 diameter; these designs are described and compared. The lowest technical risk design (with 2.5m M2) has been selected as the baseline, but the other designs have better optical quality and their perceived risks may diminish as the system design and underlying technologies mature.

Items.Authors: Anthony I. Huber, Jason Austermann, James Beall, James Burgoyne, Scott Chapman, Douglas Henke, Johannes Hubmayr, Matthew Koc, Jeffrey van Lanen, Adrian Sinclair, Anna Vaskuri, Michael Vissers, Jordan Wheeler, Ruixuan Xie
Items.Title: CCAT: characterization of the first KID array for the Prime-Cam 850 GHz module
Items.Abstract: The Fred Young Submillimeter Telescope (FYST) is a 6-meter crossed-Dragone telescope developed by the CCAT collaboration. Sited at 5600 m, FYST will provide superior observing conditions for submillimeter astronomy. Prime-Cam is a first-generation instrument designed to house multiple separate camera modules. The 850 GHz module of Prime-Cam is the highest-frequency band and is designed to deploy ~38,000 polarization-sensitive lumped-element kinetic inductance detectors (KIDs) across 3 arrays. These detectors incorporate a novel two-octave resonator network design to maximize multiplexing in an RFSoC readout system. We review the design and fabrication process for the 850 GHz KIDs. We present the characterization of the first KID array developed for the 850 GHz module, including optical and dark testing, and noise performance. We discuss the measured optical efficiency, sensitivity, and uniformity and the expected on-sky performance. The 850 GHz module will be deployed in 2017.

Items.Authors: Jonathan W. Arenberg
Items.Title: Getting X-ray astronomy down to business: facing the manufacturing challenge
Items.Abstract: Astronomy is a technologically limited science, with x-ray astronomy providing an extreme example. Advancement of the field requires ever more sensitive observations of the universe and the systems that make these measurements are by necessity novel and developmental in some way. The funders and evaluators of these new systems demand, rightly, some level of accuracy and believability in the cost and schedule resources needed. To make these cost and schedule predictions cost models are use, which are based on interpolation. This means that the novel aspects of the design of the mission have no cost history. This paper will review recent work on how to “make the case” that future systems are producible and identify strategies to collect and use the needed data to secure the funding that powers advancement of the field. This presentation is based on the work for the development of causal cost methodology over the last decade.

Items.Authors: Jonah T. Hansen, Emilie Bouzerand, Adrian M. Glauser, Bastien Rouzé, Noah Stocker, Cindy Bellanger, Thomas Birbacher, Germain Garreau, Julio Pino Jiménez, Jérôme Primot, Eckhart Spalding, Sascha P. Quanz
Items.Title: Cryogenic characterisation for the nulling interferometer cryogenic experiment (NICE)
Items.Abstract: The Nulling Interferometer Cryogenic Experiment (NICE) is an experimental testbed for the beam combiner of the Large Interferometer For Exoplanets (LIFE) space mission. Until now, progress on NICE has been confined to an ambient bench, where we have recorded progress in deep (<1e-5) nulls at wavelengths between 4 and 5µm at 300K. However, the ultimate goal and requirement of NICE is to repeat these measurements at the sensitivity levels expected for a planetary system, requiring deep cryogenic conditions at 15K.    In this presentation, we will describe the "Ice Cube" cryostat, a small version of the future NICE cryostat that is used for component and subsystem level cryogenic testing. This is interfaced with a measurement setup using a segmented aperture interferometer and a wavefront sensor. We will also describe the testing campaign for understanding the material and mounting challenges that will be faced when translating the warm bench to cryogenic operations.

Items.Authors: Riku Sato, Michitoshi Yoshida, Takashi Moriya, Chihiro Tokoku, Shinobu Ozaki, Kenshi Yanagisawa, Kentaro Motohara, Tomoya Yukino, Kensho Tanaka, Yoshito Ono, Yosuke Minowa, Yusei Koyama, Yutaka Hayano, Kumiko Morihana, Masayuki Akiyama, Masaomi Tanaka, Masami Ouchi, Yuichi Harikane, Nanae Domoto, Yuki Moritani, Masayuki Tanaka, Nozomu Tominaga, Koki Terao, Kosuke Kushibiki, Tohru Nagao, Yoshiki Matsuoka, Toru Misawa, Tomoki Morokuma
Items.Title: Development of the NIR arm of the NINJA spectrograph on Subaru Telescope
Items.Abstract: The Near-INfrared and optical Joint spectrograph with Adaptive optics (NINJA) is a  medium-resolution optical to near-infrared spectrograph designed to be optimized for  the Laser Tomography Adaptive Optics (LTAO) system at the Subaru Telescope.  Development of the NIR arm of NINJA is in progress with engineering first light  targeted for 2026. The instrument covers 0.8 to 2.5 μm with nominal resolving power of  R ~ 3000-4000. With the LTAO correction, the instrument is expected to reach a sensitivity  of 22 AB mag (SN = 10) in the J-band with a 2-hour exposure. The detector system,  optics, and cryogenic mechanical assemblies have been installed inside the cryostat.  Laboratory tests of these components are currently underway and have progressed  without significant issues. Spectroscopic images have been successfully obtained under  cryogenic conditions. We report the status of the instrument development, including  results from the tests and a timeline toward on-sky commissioning.

Items.Authors: Aurelie Magniez, James Gill-Fleming, Deli Geng, James T. Wells, David Barr, John Connolly, Tom Davies, Sofia Dimoudi, Radhika Dharmadhikari, Charlotte Z. Bond, Noah Schwartz, Ben Buky, Pieter J. de Visser, Timothy J. Morris, Kieran O'Brien
Items.Title: Polychromatic Pyramid WFS (PoPy) project overview
Items.Abstract: Advanced adaptive optics (AO) systems are required for high-contrast imaging with ELT-scale telescopes. The pyramid wavefront sensor, selected for the first ELT instruments, offers high sensitivity. However, its performance varies significantly with wavelength. While the visible wavelength range provides greater sensitivity, it has a limited dynamic range and significant optical gain effects. Correcting these variations could improve temporal errors and extend the sensing waveband, enabling AO to be used with fainter targets.  Energy-resolving detectors, such as MKIDs, offer a way to measure the entire VIS-NIR spectrum without the need for multiple cameras. The PoPy project aims to demonstrate the benefits of using polychromatic measurements. Alongside simulations, we are developing a bench with an MKID array and a colour splitter for initial testing. Here, we present the initial demonstration results of a closed loop on a polychromatic WFS and provide an overview of our future plans.

Items.Authors: Gianalfredo Nicolini, Michela Uslenghi, Serena Farina, Vincenzo Andretta, Giampiero Naletto, Maurizio Pancrazzi, Marco Romoli, Luca Teriaca
Items.Title: Time and frequency domain characterisation of the Metis: Solar Orbiter coronagraph
Items.Abstract: Metis is the ultraviolet–visible coronagraph on board the ESA Solar Orbiter mission, designed to image the solar corona simultaneously in polarised visible light and in the Lyman-α ultraviolet emission. The instrument can acquire full-frame images on both channels at a very high rate, with a minimum cadence of one second. This capability enables detailed investigations of coronal variability and fluctuations, but also requires an accurate characterisation of the instrument response in both the time and frequency domains.  In this work, we present the methodology adopted to assess the temporal and spectral variability of the response of the Metis detectors. In particular, we identify and analyse the main sources of signal variability due to instrumental effects, with the aim of quantifying their impact on the measurements and decoupling them from the intrinsic physical fluctuations of the solar corona.

Items.Authors: Stefan Kraus, Sylvestre Lacour, Mathias Nowak, Michael Ireland, Frantz Martinache
Items.Title: VLTI down to 1.0 micron: science drivers for a high-contrast, high-sensitivity 3rd-generation facility instrument
Items.Abstract: We present the science case for a 3rd-generation VLTI instrument operating in YJH bands. Extending the VLTI to shorter wavelengths opens a new window with diagnostics complementary to current instruments, giving access to molecular tracers of exoplanet atmospheres and lines probing accretion, outflows, and circumplanetary environments. Combined with improved vibration control, shorter wavelengths boost astrometric precision for detecting exomoons, searching for intermediate-mass black holes, and enabling resolved microlensing to probe the neutron-star/black-hole mass gap. High-contrast dual-field capability enables spectroscopy of giant and rocky planets from 0.03 to 1″, including GAIA DR4 and RV targets; polarimetry constrains clouds, hazes, surfaces, and stellar spin–orbit alignment. In the extragalactic domain, resolving AGN broad-line regions enables dynamical masses and reverberation mapping, in synergy with the ELT to help address the Hubble tension.

Items.Authors: Erica Lugo-Ibarra, David Hiriart Garcia, Yair Krongold, Luis Zapata, Liliana Figueroa, Sheperd S. Doeleman, Garret Fitzpatrick, Laurent Raymond Loinard
Items.Title: Integrated site characterization and environmental management for the ngEHT radio telescope project at San Pedro Mártir Observatory Mexico
Items.Abstract: This paper outlines the environmental and technical management framework that enabled authorization of the ngEHT radio telescope project at the San Pedro Mártir Observatory. Coordination between IA-UNAM, IRyA-UNAM, and the Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory integrated scientific, engineering, and regulatory analyses to select an optimal site within a national park. The site’s unique natural conditions, low radio interference, and established infrastructure consolidate Mexico’s role as a strategic partner in the ngEHT network and in global black-hole research. The project exemplifies sustainable observatory development and contributes to advancing radio astronomy and high-impact astrophysical discovery

Items.Authors: John W. Appel, Charles L. Bennett, Sarah Marie Bruno, Carol Chan, Shannon Duff, Naina Gupta, Johannes Hubmayr, Gregory Jaehnig, Matthew Koc, Tammy Lucas, Tobias Marriage, Carolina Morales Peréz, Caleigh Ryan, Jeff van Lanen
Items.Title: Detectors for the second 90 GHz telescope of the Cosmology Large Angular Scale Surveyor (CLASS)
Items.Abstract: The Cosmology Large Angular Scale Surveyor (CLASS) is measuring the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) polarization anisotropy on the largest angular scales (> 1 degree) to probe the epochs of inflation and reionization. Located at a high-altitude (5200m) site in the Atacama Desert, CLASS covers over 75% of the sky in frequency bands centered at 40, 90, 150, and 220 GHz. To enhance the CMB mapping speed, we have built, tested, and commissioned a second 90 GHz receiver with a detector focal plane composed of feedhorn-coupled Transition Edge Sensor (TES) bolometers fabricated at NIST. The focal plane consists of four modules, each containing 37 feedhorns coupling orthogonal polarizations onto two separate TES bolometers, for a total of 296 optically sensitive detectors. We conducted in-lab and on-sky measurements constraining detector parameters and key performance metrics such as optical efficiency, frequency bandpass, and noise equivalent temperature (NET).

Items.Authors: Jean-Christophe Barrière, Olivier Corpace, Olivier Cloué, Jean Fontignié, Jean-Christophe Guillard, Stéphane Jurie, Mickaël Lacroix, François Puel, Dennis Dolkens, Dirk Lesman, Ivan Lloro, Jeffrey Lynn, Niels Tromp, Joost van den Born, Daan Zaalberg, Pablo Alberto Fuerte Rodríguez, Gerd H. Jakob, Wim Pessemier, Gert Raskin, Jan Goris
Items.Title: Lifetime test of the image derotator for ELT-METIS
Items.Abstract: Complementary to article presented at SPIE in 2024 about the METIS derotator design and performances, this paper focuses on the lifetime test that ran for 6 months from July 2024 in a vacuum vessel at 70K, in the ESO premises. After a short chapter to introduce and recall the design of the mechanism and its proven performances, the paper will detail the specific test set-up for lifetime testing. Then, it will address the periodic performances verifications that have been operated to get a continuous follow-up of the mechanism behavior during the 6 months test. Performances test results will be discussed in details. Another section will highlight the main outcomes of the detailed inspection after the lifetime test. Finally, a performances overview will be given as conclusion, including lessons learned.

Items.Authors: Chao Chen, Xiangyan Yuan, Hua Bai, Shouwei Hu, Dehua Yang, Tingting Liu, Shidong Shen
Items.Title: Optical performance simulation of the 14.5-meter Optical/Infrared Telescope
Items.Abstract: The 14.5-meter telescope will be the largest optical/Infrared telescope in China which is currently under development. To allocate error budgets and ensure operational performance, we developed a ray-tracing-based optical evaluation system accounting for static errors and dynamic errors. A three-layer architecture is adopted for the simulation and analysis framework: 1) an input decomposition layer that maps various static and dynamic errors to optical component parameters; 2) a ray-tracing layer that performs optical propagation calculations on models incorporating these error parameters; 3) and an analysis layer that conducts point spread function (PSF) evaluation for co-focus/co-phase observation modes, and other imaging quality assessments of concern. The detailed specifications of the analysis framework and preliminary results will be given in this paper.

Items.Authors: Jaime Ruz Armendariz, Michael J. Pivovaroff, Julia Vogel, Vadim Burwitz, Gisela Hartner, Bernd Budau, Finn Erland Christensen, Charles James Hailey, Todd Decker, Anders Jakobsen, Regina Soufli, Nicolai Brejnholt
Items.Title: The IAXO Pathfinder: an X-ray telescope for Axion detection
Items.Abstract: The axion, a pseudo-scalar particle proposed to solve the strong CP problem, remains a prime dark matter candidate, driving increasingly sensitive searches across wide mass–coupling ranges. The International Axion Observatory (IAXO) aims to improve sensitivity to the axion–photon coupling by more than an order of magnitude over CAST, requiring high-performance X-ray optics to focus solar axion–induced photons onto ultra-low-background detectors. This work presents the design and characterization of the IAXO Pathfinder X-ray optic, with emphasis on its detailed evaluation at the PANTER X-ray Test Facility. The multilayer-coated, slumped-glass optic was measured for effective area, point-spread function, reflectivity, and throughput, validating the design through comparison with ray-tracing simulations. Deployed at CAST with Micromegas and GridPix detectors, it achieved record sensitivity to axion-photon and the axion–electron couplings.

Items.Authors: Chiara Casini, Paolo Chioetto, Alan Jody Corso, Antony Herald, Federico Landini, Marco Romoli, Paola Zuppella, Vania Da Deppo, Fabio Frassetto
Items.Title: Long-term characterization of the Metis visible light point spread function
Items.Abstract: Metis, the coronagraph aboard Solar Orbiter, observes the solar corona by measuring linear polarization in visible broadband (580-640 nm) and capturing ultraviolet images (Ly-alpha HI line, 121.6 nm). This study presents a comprehensive analysis of the Metis Point Spread Function (PSF) in the visible channel throughout the mission duration.  We systematically examined PSF characteristics by analyzing stellar images within the Metis Field of View, considering stars with different spectral properties in both unpolarized and polarimetric imaging modes. In-flight PSF measurements were compared with on-ground calibration data and Zemax optical simulations to identify discrepancies and characterize the instrument's optical performance evolution.  Results assess the consistency between predicted and observed PSF behavior as a function of star position and time, providing insights into the long-term stability and performance of the Metis visible light coronagraph in the space environment.

Items.Authors: Joseph M. Durbak
Items.Title: On-sky performance of RIMAS: Rapid infrared IMAger Spectrometer
Items.Abstract: In this age of multi-messenger astronomy precipitated by GW 170817, it is important to have instruments throughout the EM spectrum performing follow-up observations. The Rapid infrared IMAger Spectrometer (RIMAS) is designed to observe transient events within minutes of the initial detection. RIMAS is a NIR imager spectrometer (R~25, 250 and 5000) designed to observe afterglows of high-redshift GRBs in the Y, J, H and K bands. Commissioned in June 2025, RIMAS is installed on the 4.3 m Lowell Discovery Telescope located outside Flagstaff, AZ, and is now continuously available for Target of Opportunity observations. RIMAS’s high resolution spectrograph is enabled by the first instance of ruled grisms used in cross-dispersed mode for ground based NIR astronomy, and is also the first instrument to use Roman Space Telescope package H4RG-10 detectors for spectroscopic measurements of astronomical objects. Here explore the performance of RIMAS’s photometric and spectroscopic modes.

Items.Authors: Guillaume Bourdarot, Frank Eisenhauer, Simone Esposito, Benoit Neichel, Taro Shimizu, Reinhard Genzel, Stefan Gillessen, Dieter Lutz, Pauline Simonnet, Thomas Pichon, Cedric Taïssir, Quentin Fournier, Helmut Feuchtgruber
Items.Title: Towards an Extended VLTI: kilometer baseline interferometry at Paranal observatory
Items.Abstract: In this talk, we focus on the extension of the VLT/I facility to additional telescopes and longer, up to kilometer baseline interferometry (KBI). We present the case study of a VLTI-VISTA baseline, offering a 1.4km baseline with 4m to 8m class telescope in the infrared. We present the development of new solutions for beam-transportation, hybrid combination, telescope design and multi-delay tracking. With its large collecting area compatible with the surface brightness sensitivity required for kilometer baseline, VLTI is a unique platform world-wide to carry extension of infrared interferometry arrays and pathfinder demonstrations at the timescale 2030.

Items.Authors: Alejandro Antonio Luján González, Elvio Hernández Suárez, Rafael Melgar Hernandez, Alberto Hernández-González, Yolanda Martin Hernando, Paula Bañares-Palacios, Ángel Alonso-Sánchez, Adriana de Lorenzo-Cáceres, Begoña García-Lorenzo
Items.Title: HARMONI at the ELT: sub-micron repeatability in the cryogenic scale-changer turrent for pre-optics: design, optimization, and test results
Items.Abstract: HARMONI is the first-generation, AO-assisted near-IR integral field spectrograph for the ELT, covering 800–2450 nm with spectral resolutions of 3000–7000 and spatial samplings of 25 and 6 mas in SCAO and MCAO (MORFEO) modes. The IAC is responsible for the Instrument Pre-Optics (IPO), which provides multiple spatial scales across two optical levels spanning 3.2 m and includes five high-precision cryogenic mechanisms. The most critical is the Scale-Changer Turret (SCT), requiring ≤1 μm repeatability due to the large separation between optical components. The IAC has developed a cryogenic SCT with an anti-backlash gear achieving <7 μm repeatability, complemented by a magnetically assisted mechanical stop reducing it below 1 μm. This work summarizes the SCT design, performance enhancements, and results from an extensive test campaign.

Items.Authors: Jinqing Wang
Items.Title: Shigatse 40 meter radio telescope

Items.Authors: Noah H. Schwartz, Samuel Pinilla, Douglas Harvey, Charlotte Bond, Ben Buky, Gianfelice Cinque, Robert Rambo
Items.Title: Full frame denoising for pyramid wavefront sensors: simulation and bench validation
Items.Abstract: Single-Conjugate Adaptive Optics (SCAO) systems using pyramid wavefront sensors (PWFS) face significant challenges under low-flux conditions, where photon and detector noise degrade wavefront measurements and limit system performance. We present a novel image-denoising strategy based on 3D sparse representations in the transform domain, grouping similar image patches for joint processing. This approach effectively suppresses noise while preserving fine structural details, improving loop stability and correction quality.    Our Python implementation achieves real-time-capable throughput and has been validated through closed-loop simulations and laboratory experiments. Results show reduced residual wavefront error and enhanced robustness compared to conventional methods, particularly in low signal-to-noise regimes. These advances highlight the potential of advanced denoising techniques to extend the operational limits of pyramid-based AO systems for next-generation telescope

Items.Authors: Giorgia Sironi, Laura Proserpio, Giovanni Pareschi
Items.Title: The optical system for the Large-Sized Telescopes (LSTs) at the Southern site (Chile) of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory
Items.Abstract: The Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO) is establishing two sites: in La Palma, Canary Islands, and Paranal, Chile, to observe gamma-ray sky from 0.03 to 300 TeV with high sensitivity and resolution. It involves 70 air Cherenkov telescopes of various sizes. Four 23-meter parabolic Large-Sized Telescopes (LSTs) in the north cover 0.03-0.5 TeV; LST-1 is operational, and others are starting. In the south, Italy's INAF and INFN, funded by the European Community via the PNRR CTA+ Program, develop two LSTs to improve low-energy detection to be set at southern site. The INAF team reviewed the telescope design for southern site conditions, especially seismic loads. The Brera Observatory is responsible for the optical system, which uses 198 hexagonal mirror tiles (1.7 m) arranged in three coronas to mimic a monolithic parabola with cold glass technique. This contribution reports about the optical design and about the optical performance of the produced mirrors.

Items.Authors: Danielle Frostig, Phillip Cargile, Daniel Catropa, Vedant Chandra, Andrew Cline, Liam Connor, Charlie Conroy, Peter Doherty, Daniel Fabricant, Benjamin Johnson, Mark Mueller, John Piotrowski, V. Ashley Villar, Matthew Werneken
Items.Title: Boombox: high-throughput, broad-band spectrographs for time-domain astronomy on 6.5-m telescopes
Items.Abstract: Boombox is an upcoming set of spectrographs on the MMT and Magellan telescopes offering broad optical coverage (355–1010 nm), moderate resolution (R~1000), and high throughput to r=23.5 mag, designed to fill in the spectroscopic gap in the Rubin LSST era. The instrument is part of the Via survey, a large-scale fiber-fed survey, with 36 robotically-positioned fibers over 1 deg^2 feeding directly into Boombox. For this survey, Boombox is on sky >100 nights per year, driving target-of-opportunity (ToO) pointings for 10% of the observing time, enabling efficient large-scale spectroscopic campaigns and timely ToOs. Boombox’s sensitivity and broad optical coverage will expand transient classification and enable complementary science, including studies of ultra-cool dwarfs, fast radio burst hosts, kilonovae, and other rare transients. We present an overview of the instrument, including the design, optics, mechanics, and software, and report on its build status ahead of 2027 commissioning.

Items.Authors: Julie Renaud, Mary Carmen Islas Bravo, Ramón Navarro
Items.Title: Monolith tiny telescope thermal performance under space extreme environment
Items.Abstract: Through this work, the thermal performance for the space environment of the Tiny Telescope space assembly (monolithic Tiny Telescope within its housing and camera ) has been studied and demonstrated through analysis and testing. The operation environment ranges from Low Earth Orbit to a plunge in the atmosphere of the Enceladus moon orbiting Saturn.  The product design- and workmanship verification have been corroborated through an exhaustive qualification program in a vacuum and at extreme temperatures, mimicking space conditions where the telescope multispectral performance and image quality has been characterised, studied and tested. This testing is crucial for ensuring that the Tiny Telescope can operate as expected in the harsh space conditions.

Items.Authors: Jonathan Lin, Michael Fitzgerald, Yinzi Xin, Yoo Jung Kim, Olivier Guyon, Barnaby Norris, Christopher Betters, Kyohoon Ahn, Vincent Deo, Julien Lozi, Sébastien Vievard, Daniel Levinstein, Steph Sallum, Nemanja Jovanovic
Items.Title: Wavefront sensing with photonic lanterns and integrated circuits
Items.Abstract: The next generation of high-contrast exoplanet imagers will require precise correction of quasistatic, contrast-degrading aberrations stemming from non-common optical paths, the low-wind effect, and petaling. I consider how two emerging technologies – photonic lanterns and integrated circuits – may improve the state-of-the-art, yielding benefits in optomechanical stability, sensitivity, and simultaneous integration with other astrophotonic observing techniques. This work is divided into two parts. First, I cover recent experimental work in photonic lantern wavefront sensing, including an on-sky demonstration of a spectrally dispersed implementation on the SCExAO testbed at the 8-m Subaru telescope. Next, I present developments in photonic-circuit-based wavefront sensing from the AstroPIC testbed at NASA Ames Research Center. Lastly, I consider the prospects for combining the two techniques, which may be desirable for highly sensitive low-order wavefront sensors.

Items.Authors: Guilhem Terrasa, Lionel Jacques, Tanguy Thibert, Grégor Rauw
Items.Title: Door Entrance Assembly (DEA) for the X-IFU instrument for the NewATHENA Mission : development status
Items.Abstract: The NewAthena mission in general and the X-ray Integral Field Unit (X-IFU) instrument in particular are designed to address a wealth of scientific questions related to the science theme of the Hot and Energetic Universe. X-IFU provides medium spatial resolution and high resolving power by means of a calorimetric detector operated at 50mK and placed inside a 50K dewar.   To provide the necessary optical aperture through the dewar during operations, leak tightness during launch and ground tests as well as spectral filtering and IR rejection, a door is implemented on the mirror side of the dewar. In this paper, we present the contribution of Centre Spatial de Liège (CSL) to the X-IFU consortium. This summarizes the elaboration of a baseline design for the door entrance assembly and several demonstration models as a de-risking activity with the intent to increase the assembly maturity.

Items.Authors: Nicolas M. Barrière, Casper van Aarle, Alex Bayerle, Maximilien J. Collon, Bruno Menezes, Piero Rosati, Enrico Virgilli, Claire Tonsa, Andrea Mazzolari, Marco Romagnoni, Pieter Smid, Marcos Bavdaz, Bart Schurink, Mark Olde Riekerink
Items.Title: Enabling mass-produced Laue lens for soft-gamma ray astrophysics
Items.Abstract: Laue lenses have long promised to extend focused observations into the soft gamma-ray domain; however, manufacturing challenges and limited efficiency have so far hampered their realization. At cosine, we use the Silicon Pore Optics technology developed for the NewAthena X-ray mirror to fabricate Silicon Laue Components (SiLCs). A SiLC consists of a stack of thin, wedged crystalline silicon plates that are bi-axially curved to provide both radial and azimuthal focusing, while achieving high diffraction efficiency within a bandpass tunable to specific applications. This scalable process offers full control of key parameters and enables the production of highly efficient Laue lens elements.  We present the results of a two-year study funded by the European Space Agency that led to the fabrication of a demonstrator SiLC, subsequently characterized at 120 keV at the LARIX facility (University of Ferrara).

Items.Authors: Matthew Petroff
Items.Title: Overview and status of BICEP Array's BA4-90/150 CMB polarimeter
Items.Abstract: The fourth BICEP Array receiver, BA4-90/150, aims to build and improve upon the heritage of the field-leading BICEP series of small-aperture CMB experiments with a dichroic instrument observing in 90 and 150 GHz bands, to further the search for the inflationary B-mode signal. The instrument will utilize transition-edge-sensor bolometers, which will be read out using a new two-level time-division-multiplexed system and be fed via feedhorn-coupled orthomode transducers and refined cold refractive optics, with the goal of both improving systematics control and sensitivity over existing receivers. With a planned deployment to the South Pole in the 2026-27 austral summer, the instrument will populate the fourth and final remaining slot in the BICEP Array mount, completing the phaseout of Keck Array receivers. An overview of the BA4-90/150 receiver will be presented, along with a discussion of its current status and future plans for the instrument.

Items.Authors: Louis C. Desdoigts, Benjamin Pope, Max Charles, Peter Tuthill, Dory Blakely, Doug Johnstone, Shrishmoy Ray, Anand Sivaramakrishnan, Jens Kammerer, Deepashri Thatte, Rachel Cooper, Kevin Volk
Items.Title: AMIGO: Reviving Webb’s Interferometer through end-to-end differentiable hybrid modelling
Items.Abstract: Non-linear detector effects severely limit JWST’s interferometric performance, compromising the stability required for AMI calibration. AMIGO offers a different solution: a fully differentiable forward model spanning the astrophysical source, optical propagation, and non-linear detector charge migration. By predicting unprocessed detector frames directly, AMIGO avoids the precision limits imposed by the JWST reduction pipeline and incorporates detector physics within the inference process itself. Recent calibration observations have further refined the model, leading to improved visibility precision and stronger detections inside the diffraction limit. This talk will present AMIGO’s current capabilities, detections, and discuss its broader implications for next-generation precision astronomy.

Items.Authors: Tomotake Matsumura, Hirokzu Ishino
Items.Title: Overview of LiteBIRD
Items.Abstract: LiteBIRD is an ISAS/JAXA strategic L-class mission to probe cosmic inflation and the cosmic history of the Universe through full-sky measurements of cosmic microwave background (CMB) polarization. From mid-2024, LiteBIRD undertook a year-long strategic reformation of its mission architecture. This effort included a reassessment of mission requirements, instrument configuration, and the associated procurement plan, while preserving the mission’s scientific objectives and sensitivity targets. The updated LiteBIRD mission places its primary requirement on achieving the necessary map depth, enabling precise extraction of the tensor-to-scalar ratio and ensuring strong capability for a wide range of additional cosmological and astrophysical investigations. LiteBIRD is proceeding toward a planned launch in the 2030s. The mission is scheduled to enter Phase A, following the Mission Design Review (MDR) in 2026. In this presentation, we report an overview of LiteBIRD.

Items.Authors: Rishi Pahuja, Roger Smith, James Wiley, Nicholas Earley, Mansi Kasliwal, Rob Bertz
Items.Title: Thermal design and modeling of the Cryoscope pathfinder
Items.Abstract: Cryoscope Pathfinder is a 0.26-m cryogenic near-infrared telescope built to demonstrate the thermal and optical concepts for the future 1-m Cryoscope survey instrument at Dome C, Antarctica. Its performance depends on minimizing instrument thermal emission, requiring a carefully engineered thermal architecture spanning multiple cryogenic components, a large entrance window, and integrated cryocooler. Pathfinder must operate both in the lab and at Antarctic temperatures, driving a challenging trade space in radiative loading, conduction paths, cooldown time, and vibration control. We developed a transient and steady-state thermal model in MATLAB/Simulink, supported by analytical benchmarks and finite-element analysis of key optomechanical elements. Several cooling strategies and cryocooler options were evaluated. Comparison of measurements with model predictions shows close agreement, validating the thermal design and the methodology for scaling to the full Cryoscope instrument.

Items.Authors: Brian Hoff, Dallas Wulf, Mohammad Islam, Tayron Dueck
Items.Title: Dish Working Group progress toward the CHORD 512 dish core array: completion of the 64 dish Pathfinder

Items.Authors: Alessandro Fasano, Yonggil Jo, Ricardo Génova-Santos, Makoto Hattori, Shunsuke Honda, Kenichi Karatsu, Chiko Otani, Mike Peel, Junya Suzuki, Osamu Tajima, Miku Tsujii, Eunil Won
Items.Title: GroundBIRD on-sky responsivity calibration
Items.Abstract: The GroundBIRD telescope is a cosmic microwave background experiment at the Teide Observatory (2400 m above sea level, Spain), designed to measure large-scale CMB intensity and polarization anisotropies (ℓ > 6, up to ℓ ~ 300) with the primary goal of constraining the optical depth to reionization (τ). Precise τ measurements are essential for resolving degeneracies in small-scale CMB constraints on the total neutrino mass (Σmν). GroundBIRD uses a rapidly rotating telescope with a 70-degree elevation, equipped with 161 lenslet-coupled kinetic inductance detectors (KIDs), 138 of which operate at 145 GHz for CMB detection and 23 at 220 GHz for dust mitigation, all functioning at about 250 mK. This setup observes approximately 40% of the Northern Hemisphere sky daily. We present an on-sky responsivity calibration of the KIDs, detailing the effects of atmospheric and instrumental variations on detector response.

Items.Authors: Elena Ferrari, Claudio Ferrari, Enrico Virgilli, Ezio Caroli, Natalia Auricchio, John Buchan Stephen
Items.Title: Imaging capability of Laue lenses made of bent crystals for gamma-ray astrophysics telescopes
Items.Abstract: Hard X-ray telescopes for high-energy astrophysics rely on concentrating radiation through diffractive systems utilizing crystals and solid-state detectors at focal plane. Our current focus involves the feasibility of employing Laue lenses made from crystals curved to fit the lens curvature.  We estimate the aberration of an X-ray Laue lens made of bent crystals arranged in concentric rings when incident X-rays arrive on- and off-axis on the lens. In each ring the crystals are oriented in order to diffract an X-ray beam to a focus plane positioned at 20 m from the lens.  We observe that off-axis sources produce rings of diffraction on the focal plane, confirming the poor imaging performance of the Laue lens. Nevertheless by using the Richardson–Lucy algorithm to deconvolute the diffraction pattern, permitted to obtain an X-ray reconstructed image with virtually the same resolution as on-axis X-ray sources.

Items.Authors: Christian Bastin, Mathias Brach, Eric Gabriel, Laurence Méant, Sabrina Orban, Olivier Pirnay, Jean-Marc Schumacher, Laurent Wéra, Tomas Chylek, Jamie Dodge, Ben Gallagher, Arthur Mihill, Gelys Trancho
Items.Title: Thirty Meter Telescope: design of the M2 and M3 support systems and positioners
Items.Abstract: The Thirty Meter Telescope (TMT), one of three Extremely Large Telescopes under construction, adopts a Ritchey-Chrétien design with a 30 m primary mirror and a 3.1 m secondary mirror. A flat tertiary mirror enables two Nasmyth focal planes, offering a 20-arcminute field of view. AMOS was selected to develop two critical subsystems: the Secondary Mirror Support System and Positioner (M2SSP) and the Tertiary Mirror Support System and Positioner Assembly (M3SSPA). Both use passive axial support via whiffle trees, with distinct lateral support concepts. For the positioning and tracking functionalities, the M2SSP integrates a Stewart-platform hexapod for six degrees of freedom, while M3SSPA combines direct-drive azimuth rotation and tilt via a stiff linear actuator. These designs meet TMT’s stringent accuracy and stiffness requirements.    Acknowledgement: This material is based upon work supported by the National Science Foundation under Cooperative Agreement No. 2331108

Items.Authors: Shinji Miyoki
Items.Title: 4th international gravitational wave observation status of KAGRA and upgrade plan for the 5th observation
Items.Abstract: The KAGRA gravitational-wave telescope in Japan began its 4th international observation run (O4a), together with LIGO and Virgo, on May 24, 2023, following three years of repairs, upgrades, and commissioning efforts since May 2020. During this period, KAGRA achieved an average BNS range of 1.3 Mpc. The duty cycle also improved significantly, exceeding 80%, compared with 53% during the previous O3GK observation. After that, commissioning activities resumed, and KAGRA’s BNS range was improved to 7.5 Mpc as a result of multiple critical noise reductions, including suppression of suspension control noise, suspension thermal noise, beam jitter noise, environmental noise, and shot noise. On June 11, the LVK restarted the O4c observation, which concluded on November 18. LVK has now entered an upgrade phase toward the next international observation run, O5. In this presentation, we will report on the recent progress of KAGRA, results obtained during the O4c run, and upgrade plans toward O5.

Items.Authors: John D. Monnier, Qikun Pan, Sasha Hinkley, Harry Dunham, Edward Turner, Roy van Boekel, Peter Bizenberger, Olivier Absil, Gilles Orban de Xivry
Items.Title: Aperture masking interferometry with ELT-METIS
Items.Abstract: We present sparse-aperture masks for the L/M- and N-band imaging channels of METIS on the ELT. Our 6-hole design acts as an array of six ~4 m telescopes on a single pupil, with a total collecting area comparable to Keck, optimized for broadband (≈20%) filters with non-redundant baselines. Our 12-hole design acts as twelve ~1.6 m sub-apertures, conceptually similar to a VLTI-AT array but with three times as many elements packed into a ~38 m maximum baseline, providing dense uv coverage for narrow-band filters. These complementary masks are tailored to self-luminous planets, brown dwarfs, and inner disks within ≲0.05–0.1″, where AO PSF variability and coronagraphic inner working angles limit classical imaging. We summarize mask geometry, uv coverage, and expected sensitivity, and we present end-to-end performance predictions with the HEEPS ELT/METIS simulator including realistic seeing, AO residuals, aberrations, and detector noise.

Items.Authors: Jason Glenn
Items.Title: PRIMA: science and technology of a new NASA far-infrared observatory concept
Items.Abstract: PRIMA is a NASA astrophysics Probe that has recently completed a Phase A concept study. PRIMA’s exciting science case, the observatory design, and the innovative technology that enables it will be summarized.

Items.Authors: Francisca A. Solis, Ricardo A. Finger, Diego S. Gallardo, Sebastian A. Jorquera, David Monasterio, Camilo E. Avilés, Camilo J. Espinoza, Jose S. Pizarro, Maximiliano Prieto, Juan Riquelme, Franco Curotto, Leonardo Bronfman, Tomas Cassanelli, Marilyn Cruces
Items.Title: The Astronomical Radio Transient Experiment (ARTE): assembly, integration, and verification (AIV)
Items.Abstract: Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs) are extremely bright, millisecond-scale astrophysical transients with flux densities from a few to hundreds of jansky. Their physical origin remains unclear, and Chile currently lacks instrumentation to detect them in real-time. The Astronomical Radio Transient Experiment (ARTE) is a proof-of-concept radio telescope developed at the University of Chile’s Millimeter Wave Laboratory, designed to continuously track the Galactic Center with an elongated beam to maximize detection of Galactic FRB-like bursts.   Inspired by STARE2, ARTE features a single-site antenna array, an instantaneous bandwidth of 600 MHz, and FPGA-based incoherent de-dispersion. It achieved first light, detecting a solar flare of over 10,000 kJy and successfully recovered synthetic FRB-like pulses, validating its signal chain and transients detection pipeline. These results demonstrate the feasibility of low-cost, wideband radio transient telescopes capable of high-impact science.

Items.Authors: Congzhan Liu
Items.Title: A ground-based CMB polarization telescope in 40GHz band in China
Items.Abstract: We are developmenting a ground-based CMB polarization telescope in 40GHz bands, named AliCPT-40G. Following AliCPT-1 (the first CMB telescope in Chia, started first light in 90GHz and 150GHz bands in the early of 2025), the AliCPT-40G is the second telescope as part of the Ali Primordial Gravitational Wave Project. AliCPT-40G will measure the polarization of CMB in 22-32GHz and 32-48GHz frequency bands with 532 transition edge sensor (TES) detectors operating at about 180mK. The receiver is housed in a custom-degsined vaccum cryostat cooled by a dilution refrigerator. Its effective aperture is about 40cm. We propose to deploy AliCPT-40G in 2027.

Items.Authors: Thomas Schweizer, Josef Eder, Masahiro Teshima, Razmik Mirzoyan, Holger Wetteskind, Christopher Jablonski, Robert Stadler
Items.Title: Adapting the LST-North mechanical structure design for the strong Chile seismic environment
Items.Abstract: The 23m diameter LST Cherenkov Telescope for CTA is the next generation telescope for Gamma-ray astrophysics. It has been installed and is in operation since 2019 at the ORM on La Palma, 2250m asl. The ultra-light weight design (110tons) allows for ultra fast repositioning (18sec/180deg) and has been designed for powerful storms of up to 200km/h. In order to install the same, very successful telescope design with only minor modifications for CTA in Chile, it must be adapted for the strong seismic activity. Therefore, the MPP team proposed to combine the LST north design with a seismic isolation system, reducing the dynamic magnification to a tolerable level, avoiding the need for design reinforcements and use the north design as is. Here we present the proposed seismic isolation system and feasibility analyses. The MPP Munich is responsible for the mechanical structure of the LST and has validated the design with detailed FEM simulations and aging calculations.

Items.Authors: Cameron Jones, Francis Bennet
Items.Title: Fast photonic wavefront sensing using coupled waveguide arrays
Items.Abstract: The application of photonic technologies to adaptive optics provides opportunities to design systems with novel characteristics otherwise not achievable with traditional bulk-optic instrumentation. Here we present a novel sensing architecture that moves beyond the constraints of conventional wavefront sensors (e.g. Shack-Hartmann or Pyramid Wavefront Sensors), bypassing the latency associated with pixel readout and and per-frame centroiding by using direct intensity measurements. We achieve this in a small footprint device with relaxed deployment requirements by leveraging the properties of coupled waveguide arrays.

Items.Authors: Uwe G. Oberlack, John A. Tomsick, Stephen E. Boggs, Andreas Zoglauer, Dieter Hartmann, Carolyn Kierans
Items.Title: Status of the Compton spectrometer and imager one year to launch
Items.Abstract: The Compton Spectrometer and Imager (COSI) is a Compton telescope for the energy range of 0.2- 5 MeV, to be launched in 2027. It will perform degree-scale imaging and spectroscopy of the full sky with good sensitivity to polarization, enabled by cross-strip germanium detectors with high efficiency, energy resolution and 3D localization of photon interactions. BGO scintillators on the sides and bottom shield the detector from atmospheric background, defining a wide field of view of >25% of the sky. This provides a high duty cycle to transient events such as gamma-ray bursts and yields a uniform all-sky exposure for sensitive studies of extended emission. COSI’s science goals comprise studies of the 0.511 MeV emission from Galactic positron annihilation, radioactive elements from nucleosynthesis, emission mechanisms and source geometries through polarization, and multimessenger sources. We present the science objectives of the COSI mission, its current status and its path towards launch.

Items.Authors: Matteo Genoni, Hans Dekker, Stefano Covino, Roberto Cirami, Amirhossein Kermani, Marcello Agostino Scalera, Lawrence Bissell, Walter Seifert, Ariadna Calcines, Gerardo Ávila, Marco Landoni, Julian Stürmer, Christopher Ritz, Carmen Feiz, Chris Miller, Stephen Watson, Chris Waring, Joel Harman, Mike MacIntosh, Sandi Wilson, Bruno Vaz Castilho, Marcio Vital De Arruda, Orlando Verducci, Igor Coretti, Luca Oggioni, Giorgio Pariani, Edoardo Alberto Maria Redaelli, Matteo D'Ambrogio, Giorgio Calderone, Matteo Porru, Ingo Stilz, Rodolfo Smiljanic, Guido Cupani, Andrea Scaudo, Vincent Geers, Vincenzo De Caprio, Mina Sibalic, Cyrielle Opitom, Trifon Trifonov, Gabriele Cescutti, Valentina D'Odorico, Andreas Quirrenbach, Beatriz Barbuy, Stefano Cristiani
Items.Title: CUBES, the Cassegrain U-Band Efficient Spectrograph: instrument overview after final design review
Items.Abstract: The Cassegrain U-Band Efficient Spectrograph (CUBES) is designed to provide high instrumental efficiency (> 37%) observations in the near UV (305-400 nm requirement) at spectral resolving power of R > 20000 (offering also a lower-resolution R ∼ 7000). With the design focusing on maximizing the instrument throughput (ensuring a Signal to Noise Ratio – SNR– ∼ 20 per spectral resolution element at 313 nm for U ∼ 18.5 mag objects in 1h of observations), it will offer new possibilities in many fields of astrophysics: from solar system to extragalactic.  We present the final CUBES design, which successfully passed Final Design Review in July 2025 and currently in the MAIT phase, summarizing the hardware architecture and the project schedule. We summarize the optical, mechanical, electrical design of different subsystems, detailing peculiar functions like the Active Flexure Compensation (AFC). Installation at the VLT is planned for 2030 and first science operations in 2031.

Items.Authors: Charles M. Bradford
Items.Title: PRIMA: the Far-Infrared Enhanced Survey Spectrometer (FIRESS): overview and expected sensitivity
Items.Abstract: PRIMA's Far-Infrared Enhanced Survey Spectrometer (FIRESS) provides 24-235 micron spectroscopy with four slit-fed, 1st-order grating modules, each feeding an arrays of kinetic inductance detectors (KIDs).  Each band covers a 1:1.8 spectral range, so the four band cover the full range instantaneously. The gratings provide R>85 everywhere, with median value R of 140.   Each FIRESS slit is 24 spatial pixels, and each band delivers the dispersed spectrum to a 24 by 84 (spectral) pixel array.  Point sources are chopped along the slit with the steering mirror to remove low-frequency detector noise, subtract the background, and provide half-pixel spectral sampling given the hexagonally-packed array.  For high-resolution, a Fourier-transform interferometer is engaged to process the light between the telescope and the grating modules, detailed in a separate contribution led by A. Kogut. Here we provide an overview of FIRESS and the detectors, the observing modes, and expected sensitivity.

Items.Authors: Romain G. Petrov, Stephane Lagarde, Roxanne Ligi, Sylvie Robbe-Dubois, Julien Dejonghe, James H. Leftley, Farin Drewes
Items.Title: The MACADAM H0 meter
Items.Abstract: MACADAM (Measuring And Calibrating AGN Distances and Masses) is an instrumental concept uncompromisingly optimized for line differential interferometry with the VLTI in the Y, J and H bands. It features an integrated combination of chips for hierarchical fringe tracking (HFT) and chips optimized for differential phase and visibility on unresolved objects, much smaller than the interferometer resolution. Very broad band use of single mode optics is ensured by an active multichromator based on dispersed pupils on micro mirrors linear arrays (MEMS) that feeds the different single band chips and corrects for chromatic dispersion and tip-tilt. The system is extremely compact in order to fit in a small visitor instrument location. MACADAM would be an H0 meter allowing precise BLR parallax on enough targets for a decisive contribution to the H0 tension assessment. The system is self-contained but can also be used as a fringe tracker for other VLTI instruments both on and off axis.

Items.Authors: Mohit Bhardwaj, Mugundhan Vijayaraghavan, A. Ranganath Harish
Items.Title: GARUDA: India's wide-field GHz array for fast-transient discovery and radio-sky monitoring
Items.Abstract: GARUDA is a new wide-field GHz radio array concept being developed in India to open an unexplored region of the transient sky above 3 GHz. In this contribution we present the Phase-0 design, including results from detailed electromagnetic simulations of an 8×8 dual-polarization Vivaldi tile operating at 4–8 GHz. We describe the conceptual architecture of the RF chain, digitization strategy, and a transient-focused backend designed for coherent beamforming and low-latency processing. GARUDA adopts a modular and scalable design intended to support future expansion into a kilometre-scale array for fast-transient studies, including FRBs. This work outlines the technical motivations, expected performance, and development roadmap toward India’s first dedicated GHz-band wide-field transient instrument.

Items.Authors: Perrine Lognoné, Peter Wizinowich, Katy Hartley, James Osborn
Items.Title: Off-axis phase reconstruction based on wavefront sensor phase and intensity measurements: application to astronomy
Items.Abstract: Adaptive optics (AO) in astronomy is limited by the isoplanatic angle. Multi-guide-star systems expand the corrected field of view (FOV) by reconstructing the turbulent volume, but at the cost of increased system complexity. We investigate an alternative single-NGS approach that exploits both amplitude and phase information from the wavefront sensor. Building on improvements previously demonstrated in telecom regimes, we apply this phase–amplitude MMSE reconstructor to an astronomical setting assuming Keck HAKA parameters and realistic turbulence. Theoretical, noise-free Zernike-basis results indicate that intensity information could nearly double the AO-corrected FOV for a Strehl ratio of 0.3 (from 40″ to 80″). Using simulations, we assess the WFS sampling, exposure time, noise level, and natural guide-star magnitude required to extract usable intensity fluctuations, and we re-analyse experimental data to support the presence of these multi-scale structures.

Items.Authors: Shannon R. Sankar, Ryan Derosa, Joseph Howard, Jonathan Papa, Kevin Boyce, Len Seals
Items.Title: Telescopes in the context of gravitational-wave observation by LISA
Items.Abstract: The immense length scales and ultra-precise measurements involved in inter-spacecraft interferometry for low-frequency gravitational-wave observation unavoidably lead to the use of very specialized telescopes in the design of such observatories. NASA will provide these crucial telescopes for LISA, a gravitational-wave mission launching in the mid-2030s and led by the European Space Agency. In this work, we report on the role and function of the NASA flight telescopes in the context of LISA’s constellation acquisition, science operations, and precision interferometry. Furthermore, we briefly outline the near-term and future plans for development, testing, verification, and delivery of these telescopes in the lead up to integration, launch, and eventual LISA observations.

Items.Authors: Lauren J. Saunders, Sara M. Simon, Shreya Sutariya, Jeffrey McMahon
Items.Title: An upgraded frequency-selectable laser source (FLS) calibrator for CMB bandpass characterization
Items.Abstract: One of the biggest challenges for Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) experiments comes from detector bandpass calibration. Uncertainties in bandpass can severely limit our measurements by limiting foreground removal and spectral fitting, especially for galaxy cluster measurements. CMB experiments currently use a Fourier Transform Spectrometer (FTS) to measure detector bandpasses. However, the FTS is systematically limited, and improvements in bandpass measurements require novel calibrators. To this end, we developed a Frequency-selectable Laser Source (FLS) calibrator, which uses a laser with adjustable frequency housed in a calibrator that allows for laser power attenuation. Following initial testing with the first FLS prototype, we developed an upgraded version of the calibrator with improved performance. We present the upgrades to the FLS calibrator, as well as characterization of the upgraded calibrator and new laser source and plans for testing with CMB instruments in the field.

Items.Authors: Adrien Laviron, Nicholas Cannady, Regina Caputo, Abe Falcone, Yasushi Fukazawa, Manoj Jadhav, Carolyn A. Keirans, Matthew Kerr, Kavic Kumar, Richard Leys, Iker Liceaga-Indart, Julie McEnery, Jessica Metcalfe, Zachary Metzler, Nathan J. Miller, John Mitchell, Lucas Parker, Ivan Peric, Jeremy Perkins, Bernard Phlips, Judith Racusin, Makoto Sasaki, Kenneth N. Segal, Daniel Shy, Nicolas Striebig, Yusuke Suda, Hiroyasu Tajima, Janeth Valverde, Daniel P. Violette, Richard Woolf, Andreas Zoglauer
Items.Title: ComPair-2: hardware, software, and expected performances
Items.Abstract: A new gamma-ray observatory in the MeV range (100 keV - 100 MeV) will bring unprecedented insights into many astrophysical phenomena, such as nucleosynthesis processes, transient and extreme objects, and will allow new investigations of fundamental physics questions such as the nature of dark matter. AMEGO-X is a gamma-ray observatory space mission concept designed to answer these questions. Its prototype, ComPair-2, is a smaller instrument composed of a silicon tracker and a calorimeter made of scintillating crystals, designed to perform a long-duration scientific balloon flight. In this talk, I will overview the current state of development of ComPair-2, the new methods of event identification using machine learning and of event reconstruction that we will use, and the expected performances.

Items.Authors: Marta Belío-Asín, Álvaro Perez Garcia, Esther Soria, Ana Maria Marcos, Noelia Feijóo, Miguel Núñez-Cagigal, Claudia Ruiz de Galarreta, Mary Barreto, Manolo Collados, Hector Socas-Navarro
Items.Title: Optical design of the European Solar Telescope: updates after the Preliminary Design Review
Items.Abstract: The optical design of the European Solar Telescope (EST) has evolved following its Preliminary Design Review (PDR), incorporating updates such as the reduction of the Adaptive Secondary Mirror (ASM) to 37 actuators, upgrades to the wavefront sensors and cameras in the Coudé Sensing Assembly, and progress in the polarimetric calibration and illumination units. The telescope adopts an on-axis Gregorian configuration with a 4.2-m active primary mirror and an ASM generating an aplanatic secondary focal plane. Near the secondary focus lie the calibration and illumination units required for SCAO operation and telescope calibration. A dioptric relay in vacuum delivers a telecentric F/50 focus over a 127-arcsec field of view, where the beam is first split into visible and infrared arms before further divisions route the light to the instruments. This contribution summarizes the first-light configuration and the updates introduced since the PDR.
